messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: P12345 for service=canary-prober-apac. Condition: TLS handshake failures > 50 in 5m. https://pd.example.com/incidents/P12345

pagerduty: Pager P12345 triggered for service: canary-prober-apac — escalation policy: eng-sre-oncall

maria: ack — I'm on it. pulling prober logs now.

kevin: on standby. if this looks like a config drift we may need to flip routing.

maria: seeing repeated errors in prober logs: "SSL3_GET_RECORD:wrong version number" and "sslv3 alert handshake failure" to edge-apac.example.com:443. Also synthetic dashboard shows 5xx spike from APAC probes.

maria: tail of logs (snip):
```
2026-03-15T21:08:12Z prober[5231]: TLS handshake failed: sslv3 alert handshake failure
2026-03-15T21:08:13Z prober[5231]: connect to 10.4.2.7:443 -> handshake error
2026-03-15T21:08:14Z prober[5231]: curl: (35) SSL connect error
```

tiffany: any recent edge deploys or cert rotations in APAC?

kevin: checking infra deploys... there was an automated nginx config sync rolled 6m ago: ops-sync-2026-03-15. Could've changed cipher list. No cert rotation scheduled.

maria: running a quick `curl -v` from prober host: `curl -v https://edge-apac.example.com/health` returns: `SSL: error:1408A0C1:SSL routines:ssl3_get_client_hello:no shared cipher` — sending capture.

maria: uploaded packet capture to s3://redwood-debug/synth/6354321000/synth-apac.pcap (internal link)

incident-bot: PagerDuty: P12345 escalated to eng-sre-lead due to multiple acknowledgements missing from primary.

tiffany: I'm taking ownership of mitigation. kevin, can you flip canary probes to eu-fallback while we validate? That should stop noisy pages.

kevin: yes. running route switch now:
```
# pseudocmd
rbctl route set --service canary-prober --from apac --to eu-fallback --reason "mitigate synth noise"
=> route applied: canary-prober (apac -> eu-fallback)
```

maria: bumped PROBER_RETRIES from 2 -> 5 on prober fleet to absorb transient failures: `kubectl set env deployment/prober PROBER_RETRIES=5 -n synth`

kevin: confirmed route applied. dashboard shows synth failures dropping.

maria: synth failure count down to 0 within ~3m. :thumbsup:

pagerduty: P12345 acknowledged by maria (ack id: 98765)

tiffany: creating incident record and placeholder for postmortem. preliminary impact: synthetic probes only, no production 5xx spike seen in real traffic. marking customer impact: none.

maria: config diff on edge-apac (snip):
```
- ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256
- ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256
+ ECDHE-RSA-AES256-SHA384
```
Looks like an automated change removed modern ECDHE-ECDSA ciphers.

kevin: timeline: ops-sync-2026-03-15 pushed at 21:12 UTC, touched `/etc/nginx/conf.d/cipher_profile.conf`. Might be bug in sync tooling.

tiffany: plan: revert cipher_profile to previous commit, redeploy to edge-apac, then switch canary routing back. kevin, can you prepare the rollback? aim for minimal blast radius.

kevin: rolling revert now (will run a canary redeploy to 1 host then roll).

maria: note for incident doc: pcap link, nginx diff, prober logs, command outputs, and that probes were rerouted to eu-fallback to reduce noise.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: P12345 suppressed by tiffany for 30m (suppression id: 4444)

kevin: revert completed on edge-apac canary host, running rollout. expected finish ~10m.

maria: monitoring metrics: probe errors trending to baseline as deploy completes.

tiffany: tagging @ops-team to investigate why ops-sync removed ECDHE-ECDSA from cipher list — possibly templating bug. We need a followup RFC.

kevin: rollback finished, routing back to apac canary in 2m.

maria: confirmed probes healthy after rollback, synth failures remain at baseline.

tiffany: updating incident with timeline and low customer impact. assigning postmortem owners: ops-config-team + eng-runtime.

kevin: handing off to next oncall @sam for verification and postmortem followup.

sam: ack — taking over monitoring and followup. will validate that config sync tool has tests to prevent cipher regressions.

maria: thanks everyone. closing active mitigation. I'll leave notes for postmortem and link to logs. :clap:
